To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Eulerian kernels are given in terms of a simple recursion relation that is valid for any coarse-graining scheme.
the coarse-graining of the dust model can be described by a simple set of recursion relations and that it is a promising approach to study large scale vortical flows in cosmology.

coarse-grained dust perturbation theory provides a viable alternative to standard pressureless perturbation theory and that coarse-graining is a promising route to derive the vorticity spectrum from perturbation theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic approach to coarse-graining cosmological perturbations.
the development of a new perturbation theory for coarse-grained fluids that is based on the Eulerian formalism.
the development of an analytical description of the dynamics of the coarse-grain dust model that can be used to interpret results from N-body simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coarse-graining the pressureless fluid model is a viable alternative to other approaches for modelling the dynamics of dark matter in the non-linear regime.
the coarse-grained pressureless fluid model is a viable model to describe the evolution of structure formation on scales larger than the mean interparticle separation.
the coarse-grained Eulerian and Lagrangian dynamics of the dust model are in good agreement with the standard pressureless model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coarse-graining the pressureless fluid model is a promising approach to describe the dynamics of large scale structure on the largest scales.

the coarse-grained Eulerian and Lagrangian perturbations are related to each other via the same transformation that is also used in the standard fluid model, i.e. the coarse-graining does not change this mapping.
we have derived the first nontrivial corrections to the Lagrangian perturbative kernels of the standard pressure-less dust model that arise from coarse-graining.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coarse-graining the pressureless fluid model is not only a viable alternative to the standard model, but it can also serve as a bridge between the two models.

the coarse-grained pressureless fluid model provides an excellent starting point for studying the dynamics of the large scale structure of the Universe, both in the Lagrangian and the Eulerian picture.

coarse-graining is a viable and powerful tool to construct new perturbation models that capture the essential physics of a system while keeping the complexity of the underlying equations at a reasonable level.
